column1: # How big a component wants to be when it takes part in a split, and where a
# surround frame leaves room for its inner part. All numbers are pixels in the
# 15x15 reference body; they are scaled for smaller boxes. Parts without a
# preference share the remaining space by complexity (stroke count).
# Split parts always end up odd-sized (3,5,7,9,11,13), with a 1px gap between
# them: in a 15px box a ⿰ split is one of 3|11, 5|9, 7|7, 9|5, 11|3.
#   left     width as the left part of ⿰ (first part of ⿲)
#   right    width as the right part of ⿰ (last part of ⿲)
#   top      height as the top part of ⿱ (first part of ⿳)
#   bottom   height as the bottom part of ⿱ (last part of ⿳)
#   frame    inner-box insets as a surround frame: <op>left,top,right,bottom
#            several may be given, separated by spaces
#   levels   shape of the component as rows,columns of parallel stroke levels, for
#            components whose IDS does not reveal it (atoms such as 幺 or 灬).
#            Rows are stacked horizontal elements, columns side-by-side vertical ones;
#            dots and slants count half. Its minimum size is (2*columns-1) x (2*rows-1)
#            px, at least 3x3. Components with an IDS are measured from their structure.
# Run `python3 juxing.py show <chars>` to see the effect of a change.
# --- shapes of atoms (components the IDS data does not decompose) ---------------
